title: DRC, Rwanda Hold Sixth Joint Security Coordination Mechanism Meeting in Geneva
detail: August 12-13, 2026 — The DRC, Rwanda, United States, Qatar, Togo (as African Union mediator), and the AU Commission convened the sixth Joint Security Coordination Mechanism (JSCM) meeting in Geneva to review implementation of the Washington Accords. The two sides agreed to advance two initiatives to strengthen monitoring and verification on the ground, and the DRC presented its Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) plan for the FDLR, fielding questions from JSCM members. The meeting follows friction in late July over the pace of the EJVM+ verification mechanism and builds on the Doha framework's ceasefire and comprehensive-agreement track with the AFC/M23.

title: Venezuela Government-Opposition Talks Conclude First Round With Judicial Reform, Frozen-Funds Agreement
detail: August 12, 2026 — Venezuela's interim government and an opposition delegation led by Dinorah Figuera wrapped up a six-day, US-backed first round of post-Maduro transition talks in Caracas (government side led by National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez). The two sides agreed to 'initiate a process that contributes to the transformation of the justice system,' including reform of the Organic Law governing the Supreme Tribunal of Justice (TSJ), and to pursue recovery of Venezuela's gold reserves frozen at the Bank of England to fund reconstruction after the June 24 earthquakes. The agreement did not address the National Electoral Council, which the opposition also wants overhauled. Nobel laureate María Corina Machado's bloc did not participate in the talks.

title: Pakistan Makes Final Diplomatic Push Ahead of Aug 16 US-Iran Deadline
detail: August 12, 2026 — With the 60-day negotiating window under the June 17 Islamabad MOU set to expire August 16, Pakistan intensified shuttle diplomacy: Deputy PM Ishaq Dar held calls with regional counterparts and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi traveled to Tehran, while Islamabad also engaged Bahrain, Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia. Iran is demanding an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief, release of frozen assets, and region-wide ceasefires (including Lebanon and Gaza) before reopening the Strait of Hormuz; Washington is seeking compensation for conflict-related deaths and damages. Iran's security chief said Hormuz 'will not reopen until the US ends the war and blockade, releases Iran's frozen assets, and agrees to a region-wide ceasefire.' Any extension of the window requires mutual consent.
